bug_info.bug_desc: The read pipeline maintains separate FIFOs for read data and for descrambling masks, and normally pops them together with rd_and_mask_fifo_pop. In the pre-merge code, the pop decision did not always wait for the mask FIFO when a mask was still being computed. For scrambled-enabled locations that are erased, descram is 0, so the data entry is treated as a non-descrambled/forwarding entry, but a mask calculation was still started and a mask FIFO entry is expected. The old fifo_data_ready and fifo_forward_pop signals popped the data FIFO as soon as fifo_data_valid was asserted or a forwarded entry reached the FIFO output, without checking mask_valid. If the flash read completed before the mask calculation (for example because the shared scrambling/mask path was backpressured), the data FIFO popped while the mask FIFO did not, causing the two FIFOs to lose alignment. A later descrambled read can then be paired with the wrong mask, corrupting the returned plaintext and producing spurious reliability or integrity ECC errors.
bug_info.fix_hint: Track whether a computed mask must be dropped for a scrambled-enabled but erased read by adding a dropmsk bit to the rd_storage FIFO, set from rd_attrs.descramble & data_erased, and carry it out as dropmsk_q. On the FIFO output side, derive hint_dropmsk from dropmsk_q and gate the shared data/mask FIFO pop on mask_valid for such entries: use mask_valid in fifo_data_ready and in fifo_forward_pop when hint_dropmsk is set, so the data and mask entries are consumed in the same cycle. Keep the existing behavior for normal descrambling entries (pop on descramble ack) and for non-descrambled entries that have no mask pending (pop immediately). Apply the same signal and width changes consistently to all copies of flash_phy_rd.sv.
